description:
Extract shared PostgreSQL wire protocol mechanics from PostgreSQLAdapter into a
reusable Psycopg2ConnectionMixin. This refactor decouples connection management
and query execution from database-specific management logic (like CREATE DATABASE),
allowing QuestDB and other wire-compatible platforms to share code without
incorrect inheritance.

Currently, QuestDBAdapter duplicates several methods from PostgreSQLAdapter
because inheriting would pull in incompatible database management behaviors.
This mixin provides a clean path for shared functionality while adhering to
the Liskov Substitution Principle.

QuestDB uses `pg_port` (not `port`), has a 127-char identifier limit (vs
PostgreSQL's 63), and uses `tables()` for catalog queries rather than
`information_schema.tables`. These divergences must be handled via class-level
constants and overrides, not inlined into the mixin.

anti_patterns.why: they diverge fundamentally in database management, data loading, and catalog queries

anti_patterns.instead: they must stay as adapter-specific overrides.
anti_patterns.why: PostgreSQL uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE and QuestDB uses plain EXPLAIN

anti_patterns.dont: unify _validate_identifier length limits to a single constant
anti_patterns.instead: use a class constant _max_identifier_length that each adapter sets.
anti_patterns.why: QuestDB (127) and PostgreSQL (63) have different limits and unifying silently applies the wrong limit

preserves.behavior: CedarDB, TimescaleDB, pg_duckdb, pg_mooncake continue to work unchanged via transitive PostgreSQLAdapter inheritance
PostgreSQLAdapter continues to support TimescaleDB extensions via enable_timescale flag
QuestDB _validate_identifier uses 127-char limit, PostgreSQL uses 63-char limit - do not unify to one value
QuestDBAdapter continues to use REST API/ILP for its primary data loading path
execute_sql_query() helper in base/sql_execution.py remains the canonical implementation for cursor-based query execution
